review_type: independent source, contract, and focused test review

A.scope: Promotion provenance is validated before native runtime/browser startup, and CI identity remains attached to the result.
evidence: scripts/promote-ci-dev-artifact.mjs defines the schema_version 1 ci_development_test_promotion receipt, exact-source compatibility, source/destination paths, CI run/attempt/artifact identity, version, tree hash, and publication state; scripts/verify-ci-dev-promotion.mjs checks those fields against verifyImportedNativeEvidence output and hashes both imported and promoted trees.

The verifier requires the pinned source SHA, exact .output/chrome-mv3-dev destination, development extension ID derived from the manifest key, version, run/attempt/artifact identity, and exact-source compatibility. Fixed ci_dev_promotion_identity_refused is returned on failure.

tests/browser/native-sidepanel-qa-harness.mjs verifies the promotion before resolving browser runtime or creating an owned profile, compares expected identity fields, and preserves the promotion kind. tests/browser/native-ci-promotion-gate.test.mjs checks mismatch refusal and that failure stops at the receipt stage.

The capture, gallery-failure, and guest Screenshots runners route CI promotion receipts through the verifier. Existing local receipt branches and published-release resolution remain present; guest CI provenance is serialized in its before/after build identity.
A.native_product_acceptance: UNVERIFIED; this review did not launch Chrome or exercise product behavior.

evidence: Focused command: node --test scripts/verify-ci-dev-promotion.test.mjs tests/browser/native-ci-promotion-gate.test.mjs tests/browser/native-startup-interval-callsite.test.mjs; 32 passed, 0 failed.

Promotion verifier tests reject absent/wrong source SHA, mismatched receipt/import source, wrong extension ID, destination/source path, run/artifact, version, either changed tree, and runtime-equivalent compatibility. These tests call the receipt-validation function directly and confirm fixed refusal.

The startup interval VM fixture now invokes the actual extracted driver and validates the identity-routing inputs at its injected verifier boundary; it no longer supplies resolveExpectedRelease as unconditional success.
limitations: The positive/negative promotion fixtures synthesize receipt and imported-evidence objects and exercise requireCiDevPromotionReceipt directly; they do not exercise verifyCiDevPromotionReceipt against a complete on-disk imported artifact fixture. Receipt path, schema/kind, publication flags, symlink, and timestamp rejection lack dedicated negative cases in the new verifier test file.

The startup VM test deliberately replaces the actual verifier and runtime boundary. Real verifier filesystem behavior is covered only by the pure validation fixture, so this is meaningful gate-order coverage but not end-to-end native startup proof.
